title: Escape Routes
story: An explorer enters the maze and escapes across either bright end gate before the tracker wins the ball.
setup: Build two 10x14-yard fields. Mark two wide scoring gates on opposite sides of each field and place two pairs at each field.
instructions: An attacker enters with the ball; the defender starts two steps away.
The attacker scores by dribbling under control through either scoring gate.
If the defender wins it, the defender may escape through either gate immediately.
End after a score or ball out, switch the starting role and restart with the other pair.
coach_lens: Notice whether the attacker looks at both exits, moves the defender one way and accelerates into the other. For defenders, praise protecting one route while staying ready to change.
questions: How can you make the tracker lean the wrong way?

simplify: Widen both gates or delay the defender until the attacker's second touch.
challenge: Narrow one gate so the attacker must compare risk and space.
low_attendance: Use one field and alternate pairs after each short round.
high_attendance: Create another field; cap each field at three pairs.
limited_equipment: Use full end lines as scoring targets and field markings as boundaries.

safety: Keep waiting players to the side of the field, away from scoring gates.
Use standing challenges only and stop balls leaving toward another group.

diagram.alt: An attacker and defender stand between two scoring gates; curved arrows show two possible escape routes.

source.title: MiniRoos Activity Guide: Tricky Goal Lines
source.reviewer_notes: The two-choice directional 1v1 idea is adapted into parallel small fields, immediate defender counters and short pair rotations to reduce waiting. Wording, name and diagram are original SmallSide work.
